title: Senior Financial Risk Specialist – Financial Risk Management (w/m/d)
description: Du bist in den Kapitalmärkten zuhause, begeisterst Dich für intelligentes Risikomanagement und quantitative Analysen? Du möchtest mit modernen Modellen und Daten fundierte Entscheidungen unterstützen und dabei in einem internationalen und agilen Umfeld arbeiten? Eine Unternehmenskultur, die Eigenverantwortung fördert, Leistung honoriert und Raum für kontinuierliche Weiterentwicklung bietet, passt perfekt zu Dir? Dann bewirb Dich jetzt mit Deinem Lebenslauf, Dein Team freut sich schon auf Dich. Deine Aufgaben Du analysierst und quantifizierst als Teil der unabhängigen 2nd Line of Defence Markt- und Liquiditätsrisiken über sämtliche Geschäftsaktivitäten der Bank hinweg – vom Retail und Wholesale Banking bis hin zum Group Treasury – und lieferst damit eine fundierte unabhängige Risikoeinschätzung in einem dynamischen Marktumfeld. Dabei übernimmst Du die Model Ownership unserer Financial-Risk-Modelle und stellst durch unabhängige Challenge sicher, dass Kalibrierung und Anwendung angemessen sind. Modellannahmen und Kundenverhalten hinterfragst Du kritisch und bewertest deren Auswirkungen auf Zins- und Liquiditätsrisikoprofile – beispielsweise bei Sondertilgungsrechten in der Baufinanzierung. Mit Auge fürs Detail beurteilst Du Zinsrisiken, Hedging-Strategien sowie die Angemessenheit des Einsatzes von Derivaten. Durch Szenarioanalysen und Stresstests identifizierst Du potenzielle Risiken frühzeitig und leistest damit einen wesentlichen Beitrag zur unabhängigen Risikoüberwachung. Natürlich hast Du hierbei auch Risk Appetite und Limits im Auge, bewertest Abweichungen sorgfältig und eskalierst diese, falls nötig. Dank Deiner Expertise bereitest Du Risikoeinschätzungen verständlich auf und vertrittst diese überzeugend gegenüber Senior Management, Governance-Gremien, Aufsichtsbehörden und dem ING Head Office. Bei allem, was Du tust, setzt Du auf Zusammenarbeit: Du arbeitest eng mit Kolleg*innen aus unterschiedlichen Bankeinheiten und dem Head Office zusammen, gestaltest gruppenweite Standards mit und treibst die ganzheitliche Weiterentwicklung unseres Financial Risk Frameworks voran. Dein Profil Abgeschlossenes Studium der Wirtschaftswissenschaften, (Wirtschafts-)Mathematik, Physik oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation Mehrjährige Berufserfahrung im Market & Liquidity Risk Management, ALM, Treasury oder in einem vergleichbaren Umfeld Fundierte Kenntnisse in IRRBB, Liquiditätsrisiko, ALM und Kapitalmarktprodukten Erfahrung damit, Modelle, Kalibrierungen und Risikosteuerentscheidungen unabhängig zu beurteilen und kritisch zu challengen Sehr gute Kenntnisse in Python oder vergleichbaren Tools zur quantitativen Datenanalyse Ausgeprägte analytische Fähigkeiten sowie die Fähigkeit, fundierte Risikopositionen zu entwickeln und gegenüber Senior Stakeholdern überzeugend zu vertreten Offen für kulturelle Vielfalt in einem international geprägten Umfeld Sehr gutes Deutsch und Englisch in Wort und Schrift Freu Dich auf zahlreiche Benefits Betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Vermögenswirksame Leistungen, kostenloses Deutschlandticket & Bike LeasING, Betriebsrestaurant Hybrides Arbeitsmodell: Zusätzlich zur Arbeit im Büro kannst Du auch mobil arbeiten – im Rahmen betrieblicher, gesetzlicher und regulatorischer Anforderungen. Individuelle Arbeitszeitmodelle, Sabbatical, Bezuschussung von Pflege- & Kinderbetreuungskosten Eigene Budgets für persönliche Entwicklung und Gesundheit plus persönliches Ausstattungsbudget für Deinen mobilen Arbeitsplatz Bereit für einen neuen Job? Bei der ING sind wir bunt und vielfältig: unterschiedliche Persönlichkeiten mit verschiedenen Perspektiven - in einer internationalen Kultur, in der wir uns wertschätzen. Dabei tragen wir Sneaker und Pumps, Hoodies und Anzüge. Weil Menschen nicht in Schubladen passen. Das klingt ganz nach Dir? Bewirb Dich jetzt einfach online bei uns – Dein Lebenslauf reicht uns, um Dich kennenzulernen, ein Anschreiben ist optional!

Job Description JOB TITLE: Associate, Liquidity Pricing & Strategy LOCATION: London or Edinburgh SALARY: Competitive Package HOURS: Full-time WORKING PATTERN: Minimum two days per week or 40% of working hours in office/hub. Pricing strategy and governance is critical to ensuring strong client outcomes while maximising value from CIB customer deposits. The team play a vital role in supporting growth in the CIB client franchise by collaborating closely with teams across the Group including Sales, Coverage, Finance, Group Corporate Treasury, Balance Sheet Management and BCB. The role offers an excellent opportunity to develop a deep understanding of client liquidity needs, embed new tools and insights to drive growth, and play an important role in driving income initiatives for the Business. We keep your data safe. title: Treasury Specialist – Liquidity Management & Money Markets (w/m/d)
description: Why just watch from the sidelines when you can join us and shape things? You make things work and then make them a little better every day. You also think unconventionally or try out the seemingly impossible – preferably together with the right people. Ideally, in a company that values communication, learning and ambition. Does this sound like you? Perfect! Apply now with your CV – your future team looks forward to meeting you. Your Tasks In your day-to-day work, you support the management of ING Germany’s liquidity, funding, cash, collateral and short-term interest rate risk positions across various currencies, including cash forecasting, nostro account management, intraday liquidity monitoring and central bank transactions. You manage and further develop the bank’s strategic liquidity management, including the LCR, NSFR and minimum reserve requirements. This includes analysing liquidity transfers from the business areas to Treasury and executing appropriate funding and hedging transactions to manage liquidity, refixing and short-term interest rate risks. As part of the trading activities, you execute money market, foreign exchange, repo and interest rate derivative transactions within the applicable Treasury mandates and the defined risk appetite. You monitor portfolio risks, funding positions, P&L developments, financial markets, funding conditions and liquidity developments. Based on quantitative analyses, you identify key drivers and prepare recommendations to support management reporting and forecasting. You manage collateral portfolios and optimise the allocation of securities and cash collateral for internal and external counterparties. Looking to the future, you support Treasury transformation initiatives, regulatory implementations, process automation and system developments. You also build and maintain relationships with market participants, counterparties and internal stakeholders to support Treasury objectives. Your Profile University degree in economics, finance, mathematics, business administration or a comparable field Relevant professional experience in Treasury, liquidity management, financial markets, asset-liability management (ALM) or risk management Sound understanding of funding, liquidity risk management, financial and capital markets and/or Treasury products Experience with FX derivatives, money market products, interest rate derivatives, repos and other collateralised financing transactions Familiarity with liquidity-related regulatory requirements and frameworks such as the LCR and NSFR, as well as confidence in working with large data sets Ideally, experience with Treasury platforms and tools such as Bloomberg, Murex or Anvil Structured and meticulous way of working, coupled with strong analytical and conceptual skills Strong communication and stakeholder management skills Open to cultural diversity in an international environment Fluency in English, German is a plus We offer many benefits Company pension plan, capital-building offers, free Deutschlandticket & bicycle leasING, company restaurant Hybrid working: In addition to working in the office, you can also work remotely – within operational, regulatory and legal requirements. Individualized work schedule models, sabbatical, subsidization of nursing & childcare costs Personal budget for continuing education and development as well as health; plus, a personal budget to set up your mobile working space Ready for a new job? At ING we are colourful and diverse: different personalities with different perspectives - an international culture where we value and appreciate each other. We believe in substance over style, people instead of labels. This describes you to a T? Simply apply online - your resume is all we need to get to know you, a cover letter is optional!

description: Are you an experienced financing professional with a proven track record in leveraged and acquisition finance transactions? As a Director in our Leveraged and Acquisition Finance (LAF) team within RBI’s Private Markets Finance (PMF) department, you will play a key role in originating, structuring, underwriting and executing complex financing transactions across Western Europe and CEE. You will assume end-to-end responsibility for transactions, from initial client engagement and credit assessment through underwriting, documentation, syndication and closing to ongoing portfolio management. Working closely with private equity sponsors, large corporates, professional advisors and other European and global financial institutions, you will arrange and execute sophisticated financing solutions. This is a senior role for a professional who combines strong commercial judgement with in-depth credit, structuring and loan documentation expertise. Your mission at RBI: Analyze, Structure, Negotiate and Execute: Lead complex large- and mid-cap leveraged buyouts, acquisition financings, refinancings and other event-driven transactions across Western Europe and CEE, at times in cooperation with RBI Network Units. Drive Client Engagement: Conduct financing discussions, negotiations and pitches with private equity sponsors, corporate clients, financial advisors and other stakeholders. Deliver Bankable Financing Solutions: Structure commercially attractive financing solutions while identifying, assessing and mitigating key credit and transaction risks. Lead Deal Teams: Coordinate multidisciplinary deal teams across relationship management, credit risk, legal, syndication and other internal functions, acting as a senior point of contact throughout transaction execution. Coach & Develop: Share expertise, provide guidance and support the professional development of junior colleagues. Your core competencies: Experience: Several years of experience in leveraged finance, acquisition finance or direct lending, with a proven track record in structuring, underwriting and executing complex financing transactions. Documentation Skills: Proficiency in reviewing and negotiating leveraged and acquisition finance loan documentation based on LMA standards, including large-cap underwritten transactions. Financial & Credit Expertise: Advanced financial analysis and credit assessment skills, including cash-flow modelling and financial projections. Client-Centric Approach: Ability to understand complex client requirements and deliver tailored financing solutions that meet commercial objectives and credit standards. Communication & Negotiation: Excellent communication, presentation and negotiation skills, with proven experience engaging with senior executives negotiating sophisticated financing transactions. Performance Under Pressure: Ability to manage complex transactions and demanding deadlines while maintaining high-quality execution. Language Skills: Fluency in English; German language skills are an advantage. Willingness to Travel: Flexibility to travel internationally as required. title: Senior Enhanced Index Portfolio Manager
description: Please note this position is based in London and this will be the contractual location of the successful candidate, other locations cannot be considered. Senior Enhanced Index Portfolio Manager This is a great job for someone who has deep knowledge of passive equity investing with sophisticated quantitative and engineering capabilities. A bit about the job: We are seeking a highly experienced Enhanced Index Portfolio Manager to join our Portfolio Implementation & Investment Engineering team. With deep expertise in managing passively constructed equity beta solutions, the successful candidate will play a leading role in shaping the evolution of our Enhanced Index strategies, driving process innovation, and ensuring strong alignment between portfolio outcomes and investment intent. The Enhanced Equity business has experienced significant growth in AUM over the last 3 years to £65bn under management and expected to double over the next few years. The new addition to the team will combine deep knowledge of passive equity investing with quantitative and engineering capabilities, contributing to the design, optimisation, and day-to-day implementation of our strategies. As a senior practitioner, you will provide both thought leadership and hands-on portfolio management execution within a collaborative team environment. In this role, you will lead enhancements to our investment processes—refining models, strengthening portfolio construction, overseeing liquidity and cash equitisation, rebalancing, corporate actions, guideline compliance, and ongoing risk and performance monitoring. You will also drive index methodology and event analysis, translating changes such as additions, deletions, IPOs, free‑float adjustments, and sector reclassifications into proactive portfolio positioning and efficient implementation across mandates. Working closely with Investment Engineering and Trading, you will help design and industrialise scalable tools that improve risk management, liquidity assessment, portfolio construction, execution quality, and operational efficiency. Additionally, you will contribute to innovation across the wider investment platform by challenging established approaches and embedding best‑practice principles that support business growth through next‑generation automation. Skills and experience we’re looking for: Proven track record managing passive and enhanced‑index equity portfolios across regional and global markets, using advanced portfolio‑optimisation tools and an engineering mindset to deliver low‑risk equity beta solutions for clients. Deep understanding of equity instruments, trading mechanics, market microstructure, benchmark construction, index methodologies and end to end investment processes applied to managing large portfolios (>GBP 100bn). Confidence to challenge established processes constructively. Propose evidence-based improvements and ability to translate complex technical ideas into clear concepts for non-specialist stakeholders. Naturally inquisitive and innovative, with a passion for solving complex portfolio‑construction, implementation and trading challenges in a team‑based environment. What you’ll get for this role: Generous pension scheme - Aviva will contribute up to 14%, depending on what you put in Eligibility for annual performance bonus Family friendly parental and carer’s leave Generous holiday entitlement plus bank holidays with the option to buy/sell up to 5 additional days Up to 40% discount for Aviva products Aviva-funded Private Medical Benefit to help you get expert support when you need it Brilliant flexible benefits including electric cars Aviva Matching Share Plan and Save As You Earn scheme 21 volunteering hours per year In this role you’ll be ‘Certified’ under the Financial Conduct Authority / Prudential Regulation Authority’s Senior Managers and Certification Regime (SMCR). This means that we’ll need to complete some regulatory background checks on you before you take up your role and we’ll need to ask you some questions on an annual basis to make sure you remain ‘fit and proper’ and competent to carry out your role. We’ll provide training on what holding a SMCR role means when you join us and annually thereafter. Aviva is for everyone: We’re inclusive and welcome everyone – we want applications from all backgrounds and experiences. Excited but not sure you tick every box? Even if you don’t, we would still encourage you to apply. We also consider all forms of flexible worki

Job Description JOB TITLE: Associate Director, Quantitative Analytics LOCATIONS: London HOURS: Full-Time WORKING PATTERN: Our work style is hybrid, which involves spending at least two days per week, or 40% of our time, at one of our office sites. About the role We are looking for an experienced quantitative professional with strong Python and analytical skills to lead the development of pricing, credit-risk and portfolio-management solutions across Business and Commercial Banking. You will combine quantitative modelling with modern software-development practices, translating complex analysis into scalable tools that support commercial decision-making and sustainable client returns. Based within Balance Sheet Management, Forecasting & Pricing, you will help shape the methodologies, data and tools used by Client Products, Commercial Banking and Client and Institutional Banking. The role offers significant ownership, close engagement with senior stakeholders and the opportunity to modernise quantitative analytics through Python, automation and advanced statistical techniques. What you’ll be responsible for Own the methodology and lead the software implementation of Return on Risk Adjusted Capital models supporting the origination and pricing of commercial lending products. Build production-quality solutions for loan pricing, portfolio management, capital allocation, forecasting and credit-risk analytics. Develop reusable, well-documented and tested analytical code, applying version control, peer review and robust model-development standards. Use Python, C#, and SQL to work with large datasets, automate analytical processes and improve the efficiency and control of existing tools. Lead the application of advanced statistical and machine-learning techniques to identify growth opportunities, support client acquisition and deepen client relationships. Partner with Portfolio Management, Product and business teams to develop pricing frameworks, governance processes and regular pricing refreshes. Act as a quantitative adviser to business stakeholders, agreeing priorities, communicating methodology clearly and maintaining delivery momentum. Research emerging techniques and technologies, translating relevant innovation and industry practice into practical improvements for BCB pricing and analytics. What you’ll need ou will bring a strong quantitative background, sound commercial judgement and the confidence to lead technical work from initial concept through to implementation. You will be comfortable working across modelling, coding and stakeholder engagement, and able to explain complex topics in a clear, practical way. Essential skills and experience A postgraduate qualification, or equivalent experience, in mathematics, statistics, physics, quantitative finance or another highly quantitative discipline. Ideally at least 4 years of relevant experience in banking, financial services or a closely related quantitative environment. Experience developing quantitative models for commercial loan pricing, credit portfolio management, capital allocation, including Risk Weighted Assets and Economic Capital, or risk-adjusted returns. Strong hands-on Python skills, including experience developing, testing and maintaining quantitative models using libraries such as pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn or statsmodels. Experience writing modular, reusable and well-documented code, with a practical understanding of object-oriented programming. Working knowledge of SQL and experience preparing, joining and analysing large datasets. Strong mathematical, statistical and analytical capability, with the ability to select and challenge appropriate methodologies. Excellent communication and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to present complex technical analysis to senior and non-technical audiences. Knowledge of banking products, capital, credit risk and relevant regulatory or rating-agency methodologies. Desirable skills and experience Experience with other programming languages, such as C#, is helpful. Practical use of machine learning, forecasting or optimisation techniques in a financial context. Experience with multi-factor correlation models, portfolio optimisation or credit-risk model validation

title: Head of Group Business Controlling (f/m/x)
description: Would you like to play a key role in transforming financial performance insights into strategic business decisions? Group Business Controlling is a newly established (B-2) department within Group Controlling & Financial Performance Management. It brings together business-controlling expertise for assigned business areas across RBI AT Business Banking and the Group perimeter and serves as a central link between Business and Finance. In this leadership role, you will build and develop a team of about 9 people, create a transparent and forward-looking view of performance, and enable senior management to make well-informed strategic and financial decisions. You will have the opportunity to shape a new department, strengthen financial business partnering and make a visible contribution to RBI’s performance and transformation. Your mission at RBI: Build, lead and develop Group Business Controlling and a team of about 9 people, creating clarity on priorities, responsibilities and quality standards while fostering collaboration and professional growth. Establish the department as the primary Finance contact and trusted, independent sparring partner for assigned business areas across RBI AT Business Banking and the Group perimeter. Provide senior Business management with clear performance transparency, forward-looking insights and constructive challenge on profitability, risks, opportunities and strategic decisions. Lead budgeting and forecasting for the assigned business areas and facilitate structured performance dialogues based on consistent KPI frameworks, reliable reporting and actionable recommendations. Oversee portfolio analyses, profitability assessments and financial deep dives, and support initiatives relating to performance improvement, RWA and capital optimization, cost efficiency and resource allocation. Connect Business with relevant Finance functions, represent the department in performance discussions and strategic initiatives, and advance the standardization, automation and continuous improvement of controlling processes, methods, tools and data usage. Your core competencies: A university or master’s degree in economics, finance, business administration, technology or a comparable field. Leadership experience and strong expertise in business controlling, financial performance management, planning and forecasting, ideally gained in banking or financial services. Expert knowledge of profitability management, capital and RWA topics, financial KPI frameworks, management reporting and customer, product or portfolio analysis. A strong understanding of banking business models, products and financial performance drivers, paired with the ability to turn complex financial topics into clear business implications and recommendations. The ability to build trusted relationships and provide independent challenge at senior-management level, supported by strong analytical, communication, presentation and conflict-management skills. Advanced English skills; German is an advantage. You bring integrity, a collaborative and empowering leadership style, a strong focus on results and willingness to travel. What's in it for you: Work-Life-Balance: Flexible hours, work-from-home options from Austria. Global community: 75+ nationalities, English as the company language, and work permit support. Our teams thrive on collaboration and mutual respect. Career growth: We believe in continuous learning and proactive career development. Take on challenging work that stretches your abilities, attend trainings, and use new technologies to make a lasting impact. Stay healthy: Subsidized canteen, well-being programs, check-ups, and sport allowances. Save money: Discounts, exclusive banking terms, and a free public transport pass. Family support: Child allowances, gender-neutral parental leave, bilingual company kindergarten, and holiday childcare. Competitive salary: In accordance with Austrian legal requirements, the minimum salary for this position is EUR 4.206,12 gross per month under the applicable Banking Collective Agreement. The actual salary is typically higher and will be determined individually based on your qualifications, professional experience, and the specific requirements of the role. Application Deadline: Friday, 20. November 2026 (eob) If you have questions regarding our application process, feel free to check out our FAQ or our page for international applicants . Your contact: Eva Haselbrunner Talent Acquisition Team

Operate as a senior leader within Financial Sponsors, exercising delegated credit authority and deputising for the Sector Head when required. As a Senior Credit Officer, you’ll also be expected to have a broad understanding across our other Financial Institutions (FI) disciplines too, ensuring that risk is managed coherently as 'One FI Credit' team. You will act as a senior credit decision-maker, providing independent assessment and approval of lending, trading limits and internal ratings, whilst influencing sector strategy, risk appetite, policy development and portfolio management practices. You will be expected to provide thought leadership, support senior governance forums and act as a recognised subject matter expert within Financial Sponsors. You will exercise significant delegated credit authority across multiple portfolios, providing independent challenge, sound judgement and timely decision-making on complex transactions and relationships. The ability to balance commercial objectives with disciplined risk management, while acting in the best interests of the wider Group and its stakeholders, is essential. Drive the development of sector strategy, risk appetite, mandates, policies and portfolio management practices in Financial Sponsors Credit portfolio. Build and maintain trusted relationships with senior stakeholders across Coverage, Product, Risk and Credit functions, becoming a recognised adviser on Financial Sponsors risk, market developments and transaction structuring. Lead continuous improvement initiatives across data quality, controls, management information and credit processes, ensuring robust governance, efficient execution and effective use of management information. Deep understanding of Financial Sponsors, Fund Finance structures, lending products, counterparty credit risk and associated legal frameworks. Proven ability to influence and challenge senior stakeholders while balancing commercial objectives and risk discipline. Strong leadership presence with the ability to drive decision-making, build consensus and deliver strategic outcomes. Experience & Skills Required Significant experience in Fund Finance and/or Financial Sponsors credit risk management gained within 1LOD and/or 2LOD environments Extensive experience in credit underwriting, transaction structuring, delegated credit approval and portfolio management. title: Portfoliomanager:in Infrastruktur Dachfonds (w/m/x) - Raiffeisen Immobilien KAG
description: Die Raiffeisen Immobilien KAG (RIKAG) ist der Asset Manager für Real Assets innerhalb der Raiffeisen Capital Management. Der Fokus liegt auf Infrastruktur- und Immobilieninvestments für institutionelle Investoren mit einem langfristigen Investmenthorizont (Pensionsfonds, Versicherungen, etc.), wobei auch die Themen Nachhaltigkeit und ESG beachtet werden. Die Raiffeisen Immobilien KAG verfügt über eine langjährige Expertise in den unterschiedlichen Immobilien-Assetklassen in Europa. Aktuell verwaltet die RIKAG 2 Immobilienspezialfonds und ist der delegierte Portfoliomanager für einen Infrastruktur – sowie einen Immobilien-Dachfonds. Im Infrastrukturbereich kooperieren wir mit einem renommierten internationalen Advisor. Zur Verstärkung unseres bestehenden Teams suchen wir eine engagierte, strukturierte Person, die ein ausgeprägtes Gespür für Details mitbringt und sich leidenschaftlich den Herausforderungen des Portfoliomanagements eines Infrastruktur-Dachfonds widmet. Was Sie erwartet: Sie sind verantwortlich für die strategische Ausrichtung und Allokation der Infrastruktur-Dachfondsmandate. Gemeinsam mit den Verantwortlichen treffen Sie Investmententscheidungen für Dachfonds-Produkte und Investitionen in europäische indirekte Infrastruktur-Anlagen. Sie übernehmen das laufende Fondsmanagement (v.a. Portfolioanalyse und -steuerung, Performancemessung, Liquiditätsmanagement, Reporting), betreuen die Zielinvestments und bilden die Schnittstelle zu AIFM und Verwahrstelle. Für unsere Kund:innen sind sie eine kompetente Ansprechperson und sorgen für eine serviceorientierte Kund:innenbetreuung. Das Managementreporting wird von Ihnen selbständig vorbereitet und Sie übernehmen die Verantwortung für die Präsentationen in den Anlagesitzungen mit den Kund:innen. Sie unterstützen das Team bei der Gestaltung neuer Fondsprodukte für einen internationalen Investorenkreis. Was Sie mitbringen: Abgeschlossenes wirtschaftliches Studium und idealerweise eine berufsspezifische Weiterbildung (z.B. title: Data Analytics Engineer - Regulatory Data & Data Warehouse (f/m/x)
description: Raiffeisen Group IT GmbH is a subsidiary of Raiffeisen Bank International (RBI) with the aim of providing a broad range of IT services to Group RBI and the specialized institutions Raiffeisen Bausparkasse, Raiffeisen Capital Management, Raiffeisen Leasing, Raiffeisen Service Center and Valida Vorsorge Management. We offer an international and diverse environment and are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. In this role you are the analytical link between our business departments (Regulatory Reporting, Risk, Finance) and our data engineering team. You turn business requirements into precise, testable specifications and make sure our regulatory data is correct, complete and on time. Your mission: Elicit, analyse and document data requirements with business departments so they are ready for direct implementation in Databricks. Analyse and profile source data (MS SQL Server, Delta Lake/Databricks) to find data gaps, inconsistencies and root causes of quality issues. Create functional specifications: source-to-target mappings, business rules, data dictionaries and end-to-end data lineage. Define and maintain data contracts together with data owners and data engineering. Specify business data quality indicators (DQIs) and technical DQ checks for accuracy, completeness and timeliness; monitor and analyse the results. Test and validate data deliveries: write test cases, reconcile new pipelines against legacy outputs and run user acceptance tests with business departments. Support the migration of complex group reporting datasets from legacy processes to automated daily delivery via Databricks. Contribute to implementing BCBS 239 and the ECB RDARR Guide, including documentation for internal audit and supervisory reviews. Work closely with the Data Product Owner and data engineers in an agile team. Your core competencies: Several years of experience in regulatory reporting, risk data or finance data in a bank (e.g., FINREP/COREP, group or head-office reporting). Very strong SQL skills for data analysis, profiling and reconciliation of large datasets. Proven experience in eliciting and documenting requirements, writing functional specifications and source-to-target mappings. Sound understanding of data quality management (e.g., DQ rules, KPIs for accuracy, completeness and timeliness) and data lineage. Experience in testing and validating data deliveries, including test case design and user acceptance testing. Working knowledge of BCBS 239 principles and data governance concepts such as data ownership and data contracts. Confident communication with business and IT: you can challenge requirements and explain technical constraints in business terms. Experience working in agile teams (e.g., Scrum, Jira). Very good German and English skills. Nice to have: Hands-on experience with Databricks (SQL warehouses, notebooks, Unity Catalog as data catalog and governance layer). Basic Python or PySpark skills for analysis and prototyping. Knowledge of data modelling concepts (e.g., dimensional modelling, Data Vault). Experience with data visualisation or DQ dashboards (e.g., Power BI, Databricks dashboards). Practical use of AI tools (e.g., LLM assistants, GitHub Copilot) to speed up analysis, documentation and test case design. The actual salary is typically higher and will be determined individually based on your qualifications, professional experience, and the specific requirements of the role. If you have questions regarding our application process, feel free to check out our FAQ or our page for international applicants . Your contact: Eva Haselbrunner Talent Acquisition Team

description: End Date Wednesday 25 November 2026 Salary Range £0 - £0 We support flexible working – click here for more information on flexible working options Flexible Working Options Hybrid Working, Job Share Job Description Summary . Job Description JOB TITLE: Head of Economic Crime Prevention Oversight; Business & Commercial Banking (BCB) and Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB) LOCATION(S): London, Leeds, Birmingham or Edinburgh HOURS: Full-time WORKING PATTERN: Our work style is hybrid, which involves spending at least two days per week, or 40% of our time, at one of our office sites About this opportunity As Head of ECP Oversight for Business & Commercial Banking (BCB) and Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB), and a member of the Group ECP Senior Leadership Team, you will lead second-line oversight of Economic Crime risk across BCB and CIB; reporting directly into the Group Director of ECP (SMF17). The role holder will provide robust, independent oversight and challenge, ensuring risks are understood, effectively handled and appropriately mitigated. Through strategic insight and strong collaborator engagement, you'll influence key business decisions, shape the Group’s response to emerging risks and help ensure a robust, proportionate and fit-for-purpose ECP programme. What you’ll be doing: Lead Group ECP second-line oversight of BCB and CIB, ensuring economic crime risks are effectively identified, understood, handled and mitigated. Provide robust, independent oversight and challenge to senior leaders, Risk and Control Owners and other key partners, ensuring appropriate action on ECP risks and emerging threats. Influence strategic and business decision-making, bringing deep ECP expertise and a strong understanding of BCB and CIB businesses, customers, products and risks. Lead and develop the BCB and CIB ECP Oversight team, building strong business relationships and a high-performing second-line function. Provide expert advice on the Group’s ECP Risk Management Framework, supporting Risk and Control Owners in understanding their responsibilities and embedding strong economic crime risk management. Support effective second-line governance, providing insightful assessment of the ECP risk profile, policy requirements, risk appetite, control environment and evolving threat landscape. Ensure appropriate oversight, assurance and testing, using outcomes to identify themes, challenge weaknesses and drive improvements. Represent Group ECP with senior internal and external collaborators, providing credible challenge and insight. Play an active role as a member of the ECP Senior Leadership Team, chipping in to the leadership and strategic direction of ECP and helping shape and deliver the Group’s wider economic crime priorities. Why join us? If you think all banks are the same, you’re wrong. We’re a pioneering, constantly evolving business that’s shaping finance as a force for good. If you’re after a role where you can have an impact and do the best work of your career, you’ve just found it. What we’re looking for: Extensive experience in Economic Crime Prevention risk management and oversight, with a consistent track record of effective, independent challenge to businesses and senior collaborators. Deep technical expertise across AML, Sanctions, Anti-Bribery & Corruption and Fraud, with strong knowledge of UK regulatory requirements, industry best practice and the evolving threat landscape. Strong understanding of BCB and CIB, including the economic crime risks associated with their customers, products, services and markets. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex risk issues into clear, actionable messages for senior collaborators and governance forums. The ability to engage, influence and challenge credibly at senior levels, building strong relationships across the lines of defence while maintaining second-line independence and objectivity. Strong knowledge of banking Risk Management Frameworks, including risk and control assessment, risk appetite, issue management, assurance, risk reporting and governance. Strong risk judgement and critical thinking, with the ability to identify emerging issues, assess their significance and influence appropriate action. Inclusive leadership, with the ability to build a high-performing, team with varied strengths where colleagues are empowered, developed and supported within a culture of continuous learning and accountability.
